gallery.description: Near this point on Government Square (Gandhi Square), in front of the Court House, on 31 May 1900 Field Marshal Roberts rode into Johannesburg and accepted the surrender of Johannesburg from Z.A.R. Commandant, Dr. F.E.T. Krause. The Boers had been allowed 24 hours to evacuate the town provided they left the mines intact.

gallery.description: The (first) Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) Building, founded on 8th November 1887 by B.M. Woollan. The establishment of the JSE at this time made it the oldest stock exchange facility in the subcontinent.

gallery.title: File:SA1899 pg119 Hohenheim.jpg
gallery.description: First of the Randlord mansions, Hohenheim. It was designed by Frank Emley (or William Leck) and was home to Sir Lionel Phillips and his wife Lady Florence Phillips. It was the first house built in Parktown in 1892-1894. Hohenheim was donated and converted onto the Otto Beit Convalescent Home in 1915, and was demolished in 1972, but a plaque remains in honor of this important building.
